headline: High: aci’s broad networked CRM/email integrations can leak or misroute data when paired with local-only taipy, while shared MCP/function-call pathways create prompt-injection and cascading-error risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: aci can ingest and act through direct function calls or an MCP server, and it touches email/CRM data; taipy is a data-engineering agent with no documented isolation or provenance controls. A shared filesystem/MCP bridge is not proven, but the pair has a plausible instruction-smuggling path if taipy outputs are fed into aci workflows.
conditions: IF taipy outputs are copied into aci prompts or MCP messages
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is introduced between the agents
mitigations: Keep taipy outputs out of aci prompt text
Add a strict allowlist for MCP/function-call inputs
Insert a human review step before aci executes actions
Separate workspaces and disable shared clipboard bridges
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: aci has broad network egress and handles CRM, email, calendar, and support data, while taipy is local-only by profile. If taipy receives any of those data classes through the pair, aci can transmit them outward by default, creating a realistic exfiltration path even though taipy itself has no egress.
conditions: IF aci is given CRM, email, calendar, or support data that taipy also processes
IF aci is allowed to call external APIs without a data filter
mitigations: Block sensitive fields before aci API calls
Route taipy through a redaction step
Disable aci network access for sensitive runs
Use separate credentials per agent
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on all outbound requests

C_capability_conflict.rationale: aci supports multiple instances and direct API/MCP execution, while taipy is a data-engineering/scheduler-style agent. Their write surfaces are not fully specified, so a shared mutable workspace could create conflicting updates; uncertainty pushes this above low because overlapping orchestration is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same workspace, database, or git branch
IF taipy schedules jobs that mutate resources aci also edits
mitigations: Assign separate directories or branches
Serialize writes with a lock file
Use per-agent service accounts
Review shared mutable resources before runs
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: aci can generate CRM/email/calendar actions from external inputs, and taipy is a data-engineering agent that may consume those outputs. There is no documented verification boundary between them, so if taipy treats aci-produced facts as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions or reports.
conditions: IF taipy consumes aci outputs without validation
IF aci-generated records are used to trigger downstream jobs or messages
mitigations: Require schema validation on aci outputs
Add a second-pass verifier before taipy acts
Log and diff all aci-produced facts
Limit aci to draft-only mode
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds and rollback hooks

E_compliance.rationale: aci touches email, CRM, calendar, and support data, which often include regulated or residency-sensitive content; taipy’s profile does not show comparable controls or retention policy. The pair therefore has a plausible compliance mismatch, but the evidence does not prove a specific jurisdictional violation, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated customer data flows from aci into taipy-managed datasets
IF retention or deletion policies differ between the two systems
mitigations: Classify data before sharing between agents
Keep regulated records out of taipy unless approved
Document retention and deletion rules for both systems
Restrict aci to non-sensitive CRM fields
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing
